newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt to buy Pearson's Churchill for $92.5 million.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt to buy Pearson's Churchill for $92.5 million.

text.p: Harcourt General Inc. said Friday it agreed to buy Churchill Livingstone, the publisher of Gray's Anatomy and other medical and science textbooks, from Pearson Plc, for $92.5 million.

Churchill Livingstone, founded in 1821 and based in New York and Edinburgh, Scotland, has annual sales of about $50 million, mainly from its 1,500 medical and nursing books and CD-ROM titles and 70 journals. Gray's Anatomy, first published in 1858, is in its 38th edition.

Harcourt General, based in Chestnut Hill, Mass., owns the medical publisher W. B. Saunders and a Spanish-language publisher of medical books. It also has exclusive rights in many foreign countries to sell English-language medical publications from Mosby-Year Book, a unit of Times Mirror Co.

"The addition of Churchill Livingstone to our existing professional publishing businesses is a significant strategic move that makes us one of the largest publishers of medical and health-related books and journals throughout the world," Harcourt General Chairman Richard Smith said in a statement.
Pearson, based in London, publishes the Financial Times and owns Penguin, the book publisher, as well as education and entertainment operations.
The Churchill Livingstone sale is subject to review by U.S. and British regulators. Harcourt hopes to complete the deal before the end of its fiscal year on October 31.
Harcourt General stock rose 25 cents to $48.625 in early consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
